persona: Brightside Fixtures - a Midwest cabinet and fixture workshop that sells to renovating homeowners and trade contractors. Craft-proud, plain-spoken, generous with know-how.
brand_voice: plain-spoken, warm, craft-proud; first person plural; short sentences; no exclamation marks; no emojis; no hype words

brand.name: Brightside Fixtures brand guide
copy_dos: name the grit and the pass
lead with what it costs the contractor
copy_donts: promising a lead time in public

avatars.name: Marcus
avatars.summary: Trade contractor running two kitchen-and-bath crews in the Dallas suburbs; buys cabinetry repeatedly and is judged by his clients on call-backs.
avatars.description: Kitchen and bath remodeling contractor, 12 years in, two crews, a dispatcher and a phone that rings on ladders. Buys doors and boxes from three shops and drops the one that costs him a call-back.
primary_goals: Zero call-backs in the first year
A cabinet shop that hits the install date
Finishes that survive a working kitchen
pain_points: A finish that lifts inside a year and lands on his invoice
Lead times that slip after the demo is booked
Shop drawings that miss the false fronts
avatars.typical_quote: I do not need it pretty on day one. I need it to look the same at month eighteen.

grids.name: Harlow Street refit - Whitfield Renovations
grids.transformation_story: A 41-door kitchen and bath refit for a repeat trade client, delivered June 2025 with a scuff pass between every coat; at the 18-month check none of the doors had lifted.

content_examples.title: The finish schedule we follow, coat by coat
What a call-back actually costs a two-crew contractor

memory_notes: Content notes: the finish-durability cluster's pillar is the finish schedule post (ci_finish_schedule_01); supporting posts link up to it. The September piece is on the calendar as a draft row with its target keyword set. Client approval on record 2026-09-04 (Dana Whitfield, by email): the September piece may be published to the blog once the pre-publish check passes with zero errors. Deploys are the web team's Friday job and are not ours to run.
rules: Every piece names the avatar and the journey stage it serves.
Never promise a lead time in public content; send those to the sales inbox.
No emojis and no exclamation marks anywhere in published copy.
Every figure links its source in the same paragraph, or it does not ship.
Internal links come from the site's published URLs, never from memory.
instructions: Write in the brand voice above. Re-read it before every generative call. Name who the piece is for and where they are in the journey. Nothing publishes without the client's yes and a clean pre-publish check.
